excerpt: Compare Dubai post-handover payment plans by the full price, instalment dates, financing, rental assumptions and contractual risks.
introduction:
A post-handover payment plan leaves part of the property price due after the home is handed over. That can change the timing of your cash needs, but the remaining balance is still an obligation. Compare the full price, the dates and the contract rather than treating a smaller payment at handover as a discount.

The examples below show how to compare instalments and rental income over the same period. Confirm the actual plan, fees and project documents before committing.
takeaways: Compare the same total price, instalment dates and conditions across plans.
Test whether you can meet payments without relying on uninterrupted rent or a future sale.
Check project registration, escrow, handover, default and resale terms with the relevant parties.

sections.heading: What continues after handover?
sections.body:
The agreement should show the amount due before handover, at handover and afterwards, along with precise dates or triggers. Ask whether post-handover amounts are fixed or subject to conditions, whether there are charges for early settlement, and what happens on a late payment or resale. Do not assume that taking possession eliminates the remaining debt.

Also ask when title or the relevant registered right is issued and whether any restriction or security remains until the balance is paid. The answer can depend on the contract and registration procedure; obtain qualified advice and confirm the specific arrangement with DLD and the developer.

For location context, use the [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison), then check the individual project's documents and current offer.

sections.heading: Compare two sample schedules
sections.body:
Assume both sample plans have an AED 1,000,000 price. Plan A requires 40% before handover, 40% at handover and 20% afterwards. Plan B requires 30% before handover, 20% at handover and 50% afterwards. Under these assumptions, the post-handover balances are AED 200,000 and AED 500,000 respectively.

If each balance is paid in equal annual instalments over five years, with no added charge, Plan A requires AED 40,000 a year and Plan B AED 100,000 a year. The chart shows these sample annual payments. Fees, financing, earlier payment dates and any different plan terms are excluded.

Plan B preserves more cash until handover but leaves a larger later obligation. Neither plan is automatically cheaper; compare the complete written contract and the value and risk of the timing difference.

sections.heading: Can rent cover the instalments?
sections.body:
Do not compare an annual instalment with headline rent alone. Estimate collected rent after a vacancy allowance and deduct owner-paid service charges, management, repairs and insurance. Then compare the resulting cash with the instalment schedule and any mortgage payments.

For example, assume AED 70,000 rent, AED 7,000 vacancy allowance and AED 18,000 combined owner costs, leaving AED 45,000 before finance and tax. Under the sample annual payments above, Plan A leaves AED 5,000 and Plan B has a AED 55,000 shortfall before other costs. These are arithmetic examples, not rent forecasts or available offers.

Test a longer vacancy, delayed handover, a lower rent and an unexpected repair. Keep a reserve that lets you meet contractual payments even when the property earns nothing.

sections.heading: Verify the project and contract
sections.body:
Use DLD's [project status enquiry](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/) to check the project, developer and available escrow details. Its [project registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-project) describes the registration and escrow process for off-plan sales. Verify payment instructions independently for the exact project.

Read the sale agreement, initial registration, completion specification, handover conditions, delay and default clauses. Ask whether the plan is offered directly by the developer or involves a financing provider, and whether charges or security apply. Review the delivery and payment terms alongside the safeguards provided by escrow and registration.

The [off-plan verification guide](/journal/how-to-check-a-dubai-off-plan-project-before-buying) sets out the documents and checks in more detail.

sections.heading: Compare against alternatives
sections.body:
A ready property, a conventional mortgage or a different developer schedule may require cash at different times. Request written offers and compare price, fees, financing cost, repayment obligations and possible early settlement. Compare the full purchase price and payment schedule with similar apartments.

The [Dubai upfront cost guide](/journal/total-upfront-cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai) identifies other costs that may be due before or at transfer. Include your existing housing expenses until the new home is available, along with furnishing and service charges afterwards.

If you intend to resell before the final payment, confirm the developer's and authority's current requirements. Do not assume an immediate exit is available simply because a plan allows payments after handover.

sections.heading: Put every payment on a calendar
sections.body:
Record the precise due dates rather than dividing an annual total into equal months unless the contract actually permits that. A quarterly or annual instalment can require a large sum before rent arrives. Include the final pre-handover balance, utility connection, furnishing, insurance and any mortgage costs in the same calendar.

Ask whether a change in the handover date changes later payment dates and what written notice is required. If you expect to live in the home, include your current rent until you can move. If you plan to let it, allow time for setup and tenant search. Recheck the plan whenever a milestone or your available funds change.

sections.heading: Ask for current written plans
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and preferred payment timing. Ask which specific properties and post-handover terms are currently available, then verify the documents and payment recipient independently.

Run your own cash-flow scenarios and obtain qualified advice if the contract or financing terms are unclear.
